title: Cohomological dimension over an algebraically closed field
statement:
Let $k'$ be algebraically closed, let $X$ be a
finite-type $k'$-scheme
of dimension at most $d$, and let $F$ be a
constructible
$\Lambda$-sheaf, with finite coefficients as in
[sbc-def-coefficient-conventions].
Then $H^q(X_{\rm et},F)=0$ for $q>2d$, with cohomology
as in [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].

proof.text: By [sbc-def-coefficient-conventions], a positive integer $N$ annihilates $\Lambda$. For every section $s$ of the underlying abelian sheaf of $F$, $Ns=(N1_\Lambda)s=0$. Thus $F$ is torsion in the local-section sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], using the identity covering and the same $N$ for every section. Constructibility is not needed for this implication.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: finite coefficients imply torsion

proof.text: An algebraically closed field has no nontrivial finite separable extension: the minimal polynomial of each algebraic element splits into linear factors, so an irreducible minimal polynomial has degree one. Hence $k'$ is separably closed. Apply [lem-kun-03qu-sep-closed] to every torsion abelian etale sheaf on $\operatorname{Spec}k'$; it gives vanishing in every positive degree. By the definition [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd], this is precisely $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(k')\leq0$. Unlike the finite-ring module dictionary, this cited vanishing statement covers all abelian sheaves.

source.place: ## Proof, second sentence: cohomological dimension zero of the ground field; Stacks Tag 03QU, lemma-compare-cohomology-point

proof.text: If $X$ is empty, every scheme $U$ admitting a morphism to $X$ is empty, since its underlying map has empty target. By [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the empty family is a jointly surjective etale covering of each such $U$. The equalizer condition of [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] then identifies each abelian sheaf section group on $U$ with the zero group (both empty products are zero groups). In particular, termwise global sections of any resolution are zero, so [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] gives the assertion. Otherwise put $e=\dim X$. The dimension convention [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] and the given finite bound imply $0\leq e\leq d$. Apply [thm-sc-finite-type-torsion-cd] with $K=k'$, $c=0$ and actual dimension $e$: the finite-type hypothesis is given, and the field bound is step 2. It yields $\operatorname{cd}_{\rm tor}(X)\leq2e$. For $q>2d$ we have $q>2e$; by [def-sc-etale-torsion-cd] the torsion sheaf of step 1 has $H^q(X_{\rm et},F)=0$, with the ordinary cohomology of [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology].
